# Rethinking FileEdit: one source, a witness, and facts that can coexist I couldn't read the thread (`read_thread` isn't available here), so "implemented" below means only what this snapshot contains. The snapshot already has the nested proposal: `BufferSnapshot` with `ready | … ; unsaved?: Unsaved` (`packages/folder/src/edit-owner.ts:123-145`), it's documented in `packages/folder/README.md:244-266`, and every caller reads `buffer.unsaved`. I can't tell whether the main conversation has moved past that. ## My reading of what you want > An editor is text that always exists, plus the exact source that text came from. Saving, failing and conflicting describe how storage relates to that text. They are not stages the text passes through. ## The central question: these should not be one value Your hypothesis holds. For each pair of facts, every combination is a real situation: | | not saving | saving | |---|---|---| | **clean** | idle | you reverted while an older save is still running | | **dirty** | waiting for autosave | normal save, or you typed during a save | - **A failure and a retry can both be true.** The UI wants "Retrying… (disk full)". - **Storage changing elsewhere doesn't require dirty text.** A clean buffer whose file was deleted elsewhere is diverged but not dirty. The current code shows what happens when these are squeezed into one status: - **Wrong label.** Typing during a save keeps the old `saving` flag (`edit-owner.ts:1152`). The snapshot says `saving` while the text on screen is newer than what's being saved. - **Lost error.** An older revision's error is thrown away when newer typing exists (`857-860`). Typing after an error also clears it (`1153-1156`). - **Retry hides the reason.** A retry clears the error as soon as it starts (`844-848`). A five-way union really expresses a display priority. Keep that priority, but as a function the app owns, not as the model. ## Definitions > - **Revision**: a counter that goes up each time a change is accepted. > - **Base (the witness)**: the exact source that the current text derives from. It's set by a read, or by a save that landed. > - **Dirty**: `text ≠ base`. It can flip without typing: when a save lands, the base becomes the text that was submitted. > - **Saved(r)**: storage was seen to hold revision *r*, through a guarded write or a read. > - **`save()`**: covers the revision current when you call it. If an older save is running, it waits for that, then makes one guarded attempt against the base. It resolves `Ok({ revision })` for the revision that landed. Typing after the call is not waited for; check `dirty` afterwards. > - **`flush()`**: the folder-level version. It saves every dirty editor and returns detached `{ path, text, base, failure?, diverged? }` for each one that didn't save. > - **Failure**: the error from the last *finished* attempt. A later attempt replaces it when that attempt finishes, not when it starts. It is cleared by a successful save, or when the text becomes clean. > - **Diverged**: storage holds something other than the base, and the text can't simply follow it. Autosave stops; only an explicit `rebase()` can overwrite. ## Vanilla use ```ts const opened = await folder.open('notes/a.md', { schema: Note }); // Result if (opened.error) return showOpenProblem(opened.error); using editor = opened.data; // a lease; held input outlives it editor.text; // string, always editor.markdown; // the same source read through Note editor.revision; // number editor.dirty; // boolean editor.saving; // boolean editor.failure; // SaveFailure | undefined editor.diverged; // { current: string | Uint8Array | null } | undefined editor.refreshError; // ReadError | undefined editor.locked; // reason | undefined editor.replaceText(t); // Result<{ revision }, Locked | Closed> editor.change({ fields, body }); editor.revert(); // replaceText(base): ordinary input editor.rebase(); // adopt diverged.current as the base; next save is guarded against it const r = await editor.save(); // Result<{ revision }, SaveFailure | Conflict | Locked> await editor.refresh(); ``` `{ create: true }` opens with base `null`, for a file that doesn't exist yet. ## Svelte The parent handles loading: ```svelte {#await folder.open(path, { schema: Note }) then opened} {#if opened.error} {:else}{/if} {:else}{/await} ``` The editor component never sees a missing text: ```svelte {label()} {#if e.diverged} {#if e.diverged.current === null} Deleted elsewhere. Your text is still here. {:else} Changed elsewhere. {/if} {:else if e.failure} Not saved: {e.failure.message} {/if} {#if e.refreshError}

Couldn't check for outside changes.

{/if} e.markdown.fields.title, (title) => e.change({ fields: { title } })} />
